name: Quick replies
summary: An optional question and two to six short answers as chips, so the person can reply with one tap instead of typing.
use: under an assistant's message, when the next reply is one of a few known answers
a11y: A labelled group of buttons, each named by its own words; the picked one is marked with aria-pressed.

use_when: the assistant asks a question whose answer is one of two to six short options, such as a day, a size or a next step
avoid_when: options that need prices or details to choose between: use comparison or result-list
a free answer is likely: ask in text and let the person type
more than six answers: use a list or a select field in form-fields

parts.name: prompt
parts.what: the question, when the message above does not already ask it

parts.name: reply
parts.what: the chip that sends this answer

empty.how: the Smart UI renderer puts one plain 'Nothing to show yet.' line in an empty list

loading.how: the Smart UI renderer draws each marked slot as a quiet block of its size while the data arrives; the static file shows the filled part

error.how: if a reply cannot be sent, the host says so in the conversation; the chips stay

disabled.how: after the conversation moves on, the host may disable the chips; they stay readable

overflow.how: chips wrap to more lines; a long answer wraps inside its chip

long_text.how: a long answer wraps inside its chip instead of running out of it

keyboard: Tab moves from chip to chip
Enter or Space sends that answer
